title: JRE 2282 - Bill Murray
guestBio: Bill Murray is an actor and comedian. He is currently starring in "Riff Raff." Look for him in "The Friend" in theaters on April 4.
tldr: Bill Murray discusses his acting career spanning decades and his approach to choosing roles
Murray talks about his upcoming films 'Riff Raff' and 'The Friend' coming to theaters April 4
Conversation covers Murray's philosophy on comedy, timing, and what makes humor work
Murray shares stories about his experiences in Hollywood and working with other comedians and actors
Discussion touches on Murray's perspective on life, aging, and staying relevant in entertainment
Murray reflects on the craft of acting and how he prepares for different types of roles
recap:
Bill Murray sits down with Joe Rogan for JRE 2282, bringing the kind of laid-back, thoughtful energy you'd expect from one of comedy's greatest minds. The conversation covers Murray's extensive career in film and comedy, touching on his approach to selecting roles and what drives him creatively at this stage of his life. Murray's got that distinctive way of being both deeply introspective and completely unpretentious about his work.

The episode centers around Murray's current projects, particularly his starring role in 'Riff Raff' and the upcoming film 'The Friend' hitting theaters April 4. He discusses what drew him to these particular roles and how they fit into his broader artistic vision. What's fascinating about Murray is how he talks about comedy and dramatic work with the same level of care and intention, treating both with genuine respect for the craft.

Throughout the conversation, Murray shares insights about the entertainment industry, his experiences working alongside other talented people, and how he's managed to stay creatively engaged over such a long career. There's a lot of ground covered about timing in comedy, what makes certain performances resonate, and the evolution of his approach to acting. Joe and Bill explore how comedy and drama are connected, and Murray's perspective on what audiences actually respond to versus what critics might expect.

The discussion also veers into more personal territory, where Murray reflects on aging in Hollywood, staying relevant, and maintaining authenticity in a business that often demands the opposite. He's thoughtful about the pressure to keep up with trends while remaining true to his craft. There's genuine warmth in the conversation as two people who've spent their lives in entertainment talk about why they still care about doing good work.
